questions.prompt: In simple time, how many semiquavers equal one crotchet beat?
options: Two
Three
Four
Six
questions.correctAnswer: Four
questions.explanation: A semiquaver is one quarter of a crotchet, so four semiquavers fill one crotchet beat.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the rhythmic concept of the semiquaver in simple time.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a triplet in simple time?
options: Three notes performed in the time normally taken by two of the same value
Three bars joined by a double bar line
A note held for three complete bars
A rhythm played only on drums
questions.correctAnswer: Three notes performed in the time normally taken by two of the same value
questions.explanation: A triplet divides a beat or note value into three equal parts where two would normally fit.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the concept of the triplet in simple time.

questions.prompt: Why is 3/4 described as a simple time signature?
options: Each beat can divide naturally into two equal parts
Each bar must contain three triplets
The music must be performed slowly
Only three instruments may perform it
questions.correctAnswer: Each beat can divide naturally into two equal parts
questions.explanation: Simple time has beats that divide into two equal subdivisions, unlike compound time where beats divide into three.
questions.learningOutcome: Group notes into beats in simple time.

questions.prompt: Which grouping best completes one crotchet beat in 4/4 time?
options: Two minims
Four semiquavers
Three crotchets
One semibreve
questions.correctAnswer: Four semiquavers
questions.explanation: In 4/4, each crotchet beat can be subdivided into four semiquavers.
questions.learningOutcome: Group notes into beats in simple time.

questions.prompt: A learner is composing a 4-bar rhythm in 2/4 using semiquavers. What should each bar contain?
options: Two crotchet beats or their equivalent
Four minim beats or their equivalent
One dotted minim beat only
Three crotchet beats or their equivalent
questions.correctAnswer: Two crotchet beats or their equivalent
questions.explanation: The top number in 2/4 shows that each bar has two crotchet beats or values equal to them.
questions.learningOutcome: Compose 4-bar rhythms in simple time incorporating semiquavers.

questions.prompt: When writing a 4-bar rhythm with triplets, what is the main reason for marking the triplet group clearly?
options: To show that three notes fit into the time of two
To make the rhythm louder than the melody
To change the key signature automatically
To remove the need for bar lines
questions.correctAnswer: To show that three notes fit into the time of two
questions.explanation: The triplet marking tells performers how to divide the beat accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Compose 4-bar rhythms in simple time incorporating triplets.

questions.prompt: Which choice would improve a learner's rhythm before recording it for a digital portfolio?
options: Check beat grouping, bar length, and triplet markings before performing
Remove all rests so the rhythm never pauses
Use only one note value throughout every bar
Ignore the time signature and follow the title
questions.correctAnswer: Check beat grouping, bar length, and triplet markings before performing
questions.explanation: Accurate grouping and clear notation help a rhythm fit the chosen time signature before performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Perform and critique created rhythms in simple time.

questions.prompt: Which pair of notes are the two sharps in the D major scale?
options: F sharp and C sharp
B flat and E flat
C sharp and G sharp
F sharp and G sharp
questions.correctAnswer: F sharp and C sharp
questions.explanation: D major uses the key signature of two sharps: F sharp and C sharp.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct major scales on a staff with and without key signatures.

questions.prompt: Which pair of flats belongs to the B flat major scale?
options: B flat and E flat
F sharp and C sharp
E flat and A flat
A flat and D flat
questions.correctAnswer: B flat and E flat
questions.explanation: B flat major has two flats, B flat and E flat.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct major scales on a staff with and without key signatures.

questions.prompt: Which melodic device mainly moves from one note of a scale to the next adjacent note?
options: Scalic motion
Arpeggio
Drone
Ostinato
questions.correctAnswer: Scalic motion
questions.explanation: Scalic motion moves step by step through neighbouring notes of a scale.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe melodic devices used in melody writing.

questions.prompt: Which pattern best represents an arpeggio in D major?
options: D F sharp A D
D E F sharp G
D C sharp B A
D G A C sharp
questions.correctAnswer: D F sharp A D
questions.explanation: An arpeggio outlines chord notes, so D F sharp A D outlines the D major triad.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe melodic devices used in melody writing.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of a question-and-answer phrase structure in an 8-bar melody?
options: It creates a balanced call and response between musical ideas
It changes every note into a semiquaver
It removes the need for a key signature
It makes the melody suitable only for drums
questions.correctAnswer: It creates a balanced call and response between musical ideas
questions.explanation: Question-and-answer phrasing gives a melody a sense of statement and reply.
questions.learningOutcome: Compose an 8-bar melody with appropriate phrasing.

questions.prompt: In melody writing, what does a staccato mark ask the performer to do?
options: Play or sing the note short and detached
Join several notes smoothly in one breath
Repeat the whole section from the start
Hold the note longer than written
questions.correctAnswer: Play or sing the note short and detached
questions.explanation: Staccato articulation shortens and separates notes from one another.
questions.learningOutcome: Compose an 8-bar melody incorporating articulation marks.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a smoother vocal line over four neighbouring notes. Which articulation is most suitable?
options: Slur
Staccato
Accent on every note
Double bar line
questions.correctAnswer: Slur
questions.explanation: A slur indicates that notes should be connected smoothly as one musical gesture.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply articulation marks in melody creation.

questions.prompt: What is transposition in music?
options: Moving music to a different pitch level while keeping the same relationships
Writing lyrics under a melody
Changing every note into a rest
Adding dance steps to a song
questions.correctAnswer: Moving music to a different pitch level while keeping the same relationships
questions.explanation: Transposition preserves interval relationships while placing the music in another key or pitch level.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning and purpose of transposition.

questions.prompt: If the pattern C D E is transposed up a tone into D major, what does it become?
options: D E F sharp
D F G
B C D
C sharp D E
questions.correctAnswer: D E F sharp
questions.explanation: Moving each note up a tone changes C D E into D E F sharp in D major.
questions.learningOutcome: Transpose short melodic patterns to a given key.

questions.prompt: A melody in D major is transposed down to C major. Which key signature change is needed?
options: From two sharps to no sharps or flats
From no sharps or flats to two flats
From two flats to three sharps
From one sharp to four flats
questions.correctAnswer: From two sharps to no sharps or flats
questions.explanation: D major has two sharps, while C major has no sharps or flats.
questions.learningOutcome: Transpose music to a given key with the correct key signature.

questions.prompt: When transposing from treble clef to bass clef at the same sounding pitch, what must remain unchanged?
options: The pitch names and rhythm values
The clef symbol and staff positions
The title and page number only
The number of singers in the group
questions.correctAnswer: The pitch names and rhythm values
questions.explanation: Changing clef changes how notes are placed on the staff, but the intended pitches and rhythms should remain consistent.
questions.learningOutcome: Transpose music between treble and bass clefs.

questions.prompt: Which step should come first when transposing a melody to another key?
options: Identify the original key and the interval of movement
Change the tempo marking randomly
Erase all bar lines before copying
Replace every long note with a triplet
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the original key and the interval of movement
questions.explanation: A secure transposition begins by knowing the starting key and how far each pitch must move.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply a systematic process when transposing music.

questions.prompt: A learner transposes a melody but changes one interval from a third to a fourth. What is the likely problem?
options: The original melodic relationship has not been preserved
The rhythm is now in compound time
The music has become a folk song
The melody must be sung by a choir
questions.correctAnswer: The original melodic relationship has not been preserved
questions.explanation: Transposition should keep interval relationships consistent unless the composer deliberately revises the melody.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate accuracy when transposing short music excerpts.

questions.prompt: In setting text to music, what does syllabic setting usually mean?
options: One syllable is matched to one note
One word is always repeated four times
All syllables are spoken without melody
Every line must use a drum rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: One syllable is matched to one note
questions.explanation: Syllabic setting gives each syllable its own note, making words easier to understand.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain syllabic division in text setting.

questions.prompt: Why should a composer consider natural speech inflection when setting Kiswahili or English text to melody?
options: It helps the melody support the meaning and stress of the words
It ensures every word has the same pitch
It removes the need to choose a time signature
It makes all songs become dance songs
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the melody support the meaning and stress of the words
questions.explanation: Natural speech inflection guides melodic shape so words sound clear and expressive.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate natural speech inflection to melody setting.

questions.prompt: Which choice is most important when placing strong syllables in a text setting?
options: Align strong syllables with strong beats where possible
Place every strong syllable on a rest
Avoid cadences at the ends of phrases
Use only one pitch for the whole melody
questions.correctAnswer: Align strong syllables with strong beats where possible
questions.explanation: Matching strong syllables with strong beats makes the text sound natural and clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accents and rhythmic stress when setting text to music.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of cadential points when setting a stanza to music?
options: They mark musical resting places that suit phrase endings
They force every phrase to start with a triplet
They make all notes detached
They show the number of costumes needed
questions.correctAnswer: They mark musical resting places that suit phrase endings
questions.explanation: Cadential points help the music pause or settle where the text also completes an idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Use cadential points appropriately in text setting.

questions.prompt: A learner sets the word 'education' to only one short note. What is the clearest weakness?
options: The word has several syllables that need clearer treatment
The word must always be whispered
The rhythm has too many bar lines
The key signature is automatically wrong
questions.correctAnswer: The word has several syllables that need clearer treatment
questions.explanation: Multi-syllable words usually need enough notes or a suitable rhythm for the syllables to be understood.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse clarity of syllabic division in text setting.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports creating an original melody for a short school motto?
options: Divide the text into syllables, mark stresses, choose metre, then shape phrase endings
Choose costumes before reading the words
Write random notes first and add words later without checking stress
Use only repeated semibreves in every bar
questions.correctAnswer: Divide the text into syllables, mark stresses, choose metre, then shape phrase endings
questions.explanation: A clear process helps the music fit the words, metre, and phrase meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a text setting using syllabic division, accents, rhythm, and cadential points.

questions.prompt: Which interval is generally suitable as a consonant interval in Grade 10 two-part harmony guidelines?
options: Major third
Augmented fourth
Minor second
Major seventh
questions.correctAnswer: Major third
questions.explanation: The major third is a consonant interval often used to create pleasant two-part harmony.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify consonant intervals used in two-part harmony.

questions.prompt: Which beginning is acceptable for a simple two-part harmony exercise?
options: Unison, fifth, or octave
Minor second only
Tritone only
Any random cluster
questions.correctAnswer: Unison, fifth, or octave
questions.explanation: Grade 10 guidelines allow a two-part harmony to begin with stable intervals such as unison, fifth, or octave.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline guidelines for creating two-part harmony.

questions.prompt: In note-to-note two-part writing, what does note-to-note mean?
options: Each melody note is matched by one harmony note
One harmony note lasts for the entire song
Every second note must be a rest
The two parts must sing identical words only
questions.correctAnswer: Each melody note is matched by one harmony note
questions.explanation: Note-to-note harmony pairs each note in one part with a note in the other part.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply note-to-note motion when creating a second part.

questions.prompt: Which motion gives two independent parts a stronger sense of melodic independence?
options: Contrary motion between the parts
Both parts staying on one repeated pitch always
Both parts moving in parallel octaves throughout
One part copying the title of the song
questions.correctAnswer: Contrary motion between the parts
questions.explanation: Contrary motion helps the two lines move independently while still forming harmony.
questions.learningOutcome: Use motion choices to compose a second part to a melody.

questions.prompt: Why is ending a two-part harmony on a unison or octave often effective?
options: It gives the cadence a stable and settled close
It makes the piece change language
It removes all consonant intervals from the exercise
It prevents singers from breathing
questions.correctAnswer: It gives the cadence a stable and settled close
questions.explanation: Unisons and octaves are stable intervals that can make an ending sound complete.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ending guidelines in two-part harmony.

questions.prompt: A second part creates many harsh seconds against the melody. What revision best fits Grade 10 harmony guidelines?
options: Replace some seconds with consonant thirds, sixths, fifths, or octaves
Make both parts ignore the key
Add more seconds at every cadence
Remove the melody and leave only rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: Replace some seconds with consonant thirds, sixths, fifths, or octaves
questions.explanation: Using more consonant intervals improves the clarity and stability of the two-part harmony.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate and improve a composed second part.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of music notation software?
options: To write, edit, play back, save, and print music scores
To replace all performance practice
To turn every song into a video game
To make instruments unnecessary in school
questions.correctAnswer: To write, edit, play back, save, and print music scores
questions.explanation: Notation software helps learners create and manage written music digitally.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the uses of music notation software.

questions.prompt: Which file type is commonly useful when exporting performance data from notation software?
options: MIDI
TXT only
ZIP as a melody symbol
CSV for dance costumes
questions.correctAnswer: MIDI
questions.explanation: MIDI stores musical performance data such as pitch and duration for playback or editing.
questions.learningOutcome: Save or export music from notation software in suitable formats.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner use playback after keying an 8-bar melody into notation software?
options: To check pitch, rhythm, and phrase flow before saving the score
To make the computer compose every future melody
To remove the need for proofreading
To change the subject from music to typing
questions.correctAnswer: To check pitch, rhythm, and phrase flow before saving the score
questions.explanation: Playback helps learners notice errors and refine the music before sharing or printing.
questions.learningOutcome: Use playback and editing tools in music notation software.

questions.prompt: Which task best shows responsible use of notation software in a Grade 10 music project?
options: Saving original work with a clear file name and acknowledging borrowed material
Copying another learner's melody and submitting it unchanged
Sharing login details with the whole class
Deleting the source of every borrowed tune
questions.correctAnswer: Saving original work with a clear file name and acknowledging borrowed material
questions.explanation: Responsible digital work protects files, respects ownership, and supports honest learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Use digital tools responsibly when creating and sharing music.

questions.prompt: A learner has entered a D major scale but hears C natural during playback. What is the most likely notation issue?
options: The key signature or accidental for C sharp was omitted
The tempo is too fast for the computer
The scale has too many bar lines
The file was saved as a PDF
questions.correctAnswer: The key signature or accidental for C sharp was omitted
questions.explanation: D major requires C sharp, so C natural suggests a missing key signature or accidental.
questions.learningOutcome: Edit digital notation for accuracy in scales and melodies.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best supports transcribing a two-part harmony using notation software?
options: Set key and time signatures, enter both parts, play back, edit, then save or export
Export first, then choose a key, then delete one part
Record a dance video before opening a score
Choose random clefs after printing
questions.correctAnswer: Set key and time signatures, enter both parts, play back, edit, then save or export
questions.explanation: This workflow keeps the digital score organised and allows checking before the final version is shared.
questions.learningOutcome: Transcribe and refine scales, melodies, intervals, and two-part harmony using notation software.

questions.prompt: Which list contains the main elements often used to analyse dance movement?
options: Body, action, space, time, and energy
Clef, key, ledger, bar, and accidental
Pitch, scale, chord, cadence, and clef
Page, margin, font, title, and footer
questions.correctAnswer: Body, action, space, time, and energy
questions.explanation: These elements help describe what the body does, where it moves, when it moves, and with what quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe elements of dance used in production.

questions.prompt: What is choreography in a dance production?
options: The planned arrangement of movements in a dance
The tuning of a string instrument
The written key signature of a song
The printed programme for the audience only
questions.correctAnswer: The planned arrangement of movements in a dance
questions.explanation: Choreography organises movements, patterns, and expressive ideas into a dance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain choreography as part of dance creation.

questions.prompt: Why are props and costumes planned during dance production?
options: They support character, setting, and meaning without distracting from movement
They replace rehearsal completely
They determine the key signature of the music
They make every dance last the same number of minutes
questions.correctAnswer: They support character, setting, and meaning without distracting from movement
questions.explanation: Props and costumes should strengthen the dance idea while allowing safe and clear performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Select props and costumes suitable for a dance production.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows safe use of space during a group dance rehearsal?
options: Marking movement pathways so dancers avoid collisions
Adding more dancers than the room can hold
Using slippery props for every movement
Facing away from the group leader throughout
questions.correctAnswer: Marking movement pathways so dancers avoid collisions
questions.explanation: Clear pathways help dancers use space safely and maintain group coordination.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe use of space in dance production.

questions.prompt: A dance about water conservation begins with wasteful actions and ends with community cleanup. Which production element is most clearly described?
options: Storyline
Key signature
Clef change
Arpeggio pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Storyline
questions.explanation: A storyline organises the dance into a sequence of ideas or events that the audience can follow.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a dance storyline based on a community issue.

questions.prompt: Which rehearsal choice best improves a new dance production before performance?
options: Record a run-through, review timing and spacing, then adjust weak sections
Change the theme after every rehearsal
Ignore feedback from peers
Perform only the opening movement repeatedly
questions.correctAnswer: Record a run-through, review timing and spacing, then adjust weak sections
questions.explanation: Reviewing a rehearsal helps dancers refine timing, spacing, transitions, and expression.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate and refine a dance production through rehearsal.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports creating a short dance production for a school arts day?
options: Choose a theme, build a storyline, choreograph movements, plan costumes, rehearse, and refine
Select costumes first and avoid movement planning
Write only a title and leave all movement to chance
Use the same formation without considering the stage
questions.correctAnswer: Choose a theme, build a storyline, choreograph movements, plan costumes, rehearse, and refine
questions.explanation: A complete production process connects idea, movement, visual choices, rehearsal, and improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create and organise a dance production from concept to performance.

questions.prompt: Which feature is common in many Kenyan folk songs?
options: Call-and-response between leader and group
Silent performance without rhythm
Only written notation with no movement
A fixed piano accompaniment in every song
questions.correctAnswer: Call-and-response between leader and group
questions.explanation: Many Kenyan folk songs use a solo leader and group response as part of communal performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe characteristics of Kenyan folk songs.

questions.prompt: Why should performers understand the occasion linked to a Kenyan folk song?
options: The occasion guides style, movement, text meaning, and performance mood
It changes all songs into Western arias
It removes the need for rehearsal
It decides the number of pages in the score
questions.correctAnswer: The occasion guides style, movement, text meaning, and performance mood
questions.explanation: Context helps performers make choices that respect the song's purpose and expressive character.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate Kenyan folk songs to their performance contexts.

questions.prompt: Which preparation is most ethical when learning a folk song from a community resource person?
options: Acknowledge the source and learn the song's context respectfully
Change the meaning without asking questions
Claim the song as personally composed
Ignore pronunciation because movement is enough
questions.correctAnswer: Acknowledge the source and learn the song's context respectfully
questions.explanation: Acknowledging sources and learning context supports integrity and cultural respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare Kenyan folk songs for performance with cultural respect.

questions.prompt: A class folk-song performance lacks clear entries after the soloist. Which skill should the group improve first?
options: Cue watching and response timing
Changing all lyrics to nonsense syllables
Adding random costumes
Removing the soloist completely
questions.correctAnswer: Cue watching and response timing
questions.explanation: In call-and-response performance, clear cues and accurate timing help the group enter together.
questions.learningOutcome: Perform Kenyan folk songs using appropriate ensemble techniques.

questions.prompt: Which choice best supports a strong Kenyan folk-song presentation?
options: Clear diction, suitable movement, balanced accompaniment, and expressive group response
Very loud singing that covers all words
Random movement unrelated to the text
A tempo that changes without performer agreement
questions.correctAnswer: Clear diction, suitable movement, balanced accompaniment, and expressive group response
questions.explanation: A strong presentation combines vocal clarity, movement, accompaniment, and ensemble awareness.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply performance techniques in Kenyan folk-song presentation.

questions.prompt: How can a learner adapt a folk song for a school event while respecting its origin?
options: Keep the core style and message while making practical changes for the school stage
Remove all cultural references and invent a false origin
Turn every response into a solo aria
Use unrelated dance movements to make it longer
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the core style and message while making practical changes for the school stage
questions.explanation: Thoughtful adaptation balances performance needs with respect for the song's source and purpose.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an appropriate school-stage arrangement of a Kenyan folk song.

questions.prompt: Which feedback is most useful after a folk-song performance?
options: The response entries were late, so the group should practise watching the leader's cue
The song was bad because I disliked it
The class should never sing folk songs again
The costumes mattered more than all singing
questions.correctAnswer: The response entries were late, so the group should practise watching the leader's cue
questions.explanation: Useful feedback identifies a specific issue and suggests a practical improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate performances by self and others respectfully.

questions.prompt: Which skill is essential for clear singing in a Western style solo song?
options: Breath control
Random shouting
Ignoring vowel shape
Covering the mouth while singing
questions.correctAnswer: Breath control
questions.explanation: Breath control supports tone, phrasing, and steady vocal production.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify vocal techniques used in Western solo-song performance.

questions.prompt: Why should a solo singer study the text before performing a Western style song?
options: To shape phrasing, diction, expression, and interpretation
To avoid learning the melody
To make every phrase the same volume
To replace singing with speaking
questions.correctAnswer: To shape phrasing, diction, expression, and interpretation
questions.explanation: Understanding the text helps a singer communicate meaning through musical choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare Western solo songs using text and expression.

questions.prompt: Which performance habit best protects the voice before singing an aria or solo song?
options: Gentle warm-ups and healthy breath support
Singing the highest notes loudly without preparation
Skipping water for the whole day
Forcing the voice when tired
questions.correctAnswer: Gentle warm-ups and healthy breath support
questions.explanation: Warm-ups and supported breathing prepare the voice and reduce strain.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply healthy preparation habits for solo singing.

questions.prompt: A solo singer runs out of breath before every phrase ending. Which rehearsal focus is most useful?
options: Marking breathing points that match the musical phrases
Singing faster without planning
Removing all consonants from the text
Changing the song to a dance only
questions.correctAnswer: Marking breathing points that match the musical phrases
questions.explanation: Planned breathing helps the singer sustain phrases and communicate the music clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use phrasing and breathing techniques in solo-song performance.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows integrity when selecting a Western solo song from an online source?
options: Use a permitted source and acknowledge the composer or publisher
Download anything and erase the composer's name
Pretend to have written the song
Share paid files publicly without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Use a permitted source and acknowledge the composer or publisher
questions.explanation: Ethical performance preparation respects copyright, permissions, and source acknowledgement.
questions.learningOutcome: Source and acknowledge solo-song material responsibly.

questions.prompt: Which observation gives the best performance critique for a Western solo song?
options: The diction was clear, but the final phrase needed steadier breath support
The singer's shoes were the only important feature
The song should not have any dynamics
The performer should avoid all eye contact forever
questions.correctAnswer: The diction was clear, but the final phrase needed steadier breath support
questions.explanation: A useful critique is specific, balanced, and connected to performance technique.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate solo-song performances respectfully.

questions.prompt: Which rehearsal plan best prepares a Western style solo song for performance?
options: Learn notes and text, mark breaths, practise diction and dynamics, record, review, and refine
Memorise only the first line and ignore the accompaniment
Sing once on performance day without warming up
Change the melody at random whenever it is difficult
questions.correctAnswer: Learn notes and text, mark breaths, practise diction and dynamics, record, review, and refine
questions.explanation: A structured rehearsal plan develops technical control and expressive confidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan and refine a Western solo-song performance.

questions.prompt: Which Kenyan indigenous instrument is classified as a lyre?
options: Nyatiti
Trumpet
Piano
Clarinet
questions.correctAnswer: Nyatiti
questions.explanation: The nyatiti is a Kenyan lyre associated with plucked strings.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of Kenyan indigenous musical instruments.

questions.prompt: How does a drum mainly produce sound?
options: A stretched membrane vibrates when struck
A reed vibrates inside a mouthpiece
A string is bowed across a bridge
Air vibrates inside a metal tube only
questions.correctAnswer: A stretched membrane vibrates when struck
questions.explanation: Drums produce sound when their stretched skins or membranes vibrate after being struck.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain sound production on selected indigenous instruments.

questions.prompt: How does a fiddle such as the orutu mainly produce sound?
options: A vibrating string is bowed or plucked
A membrane is struck with sticks
Metal keys are pressed to trigger speakers
Air is blown through a brass mouthpiece
questions.correctAnswer: A vibrating string is bowed or plucked
questions.explanation: Fiddles produce sound through vibrating strings, often set in motion by a bow.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain sound production on selected indigenous instruments.

questions.prompt: Which action best supports proper maintenance of a Kenyan indigenous instrument after use?
options: Clean it, store it safely, and protect it from dampness or damage
Leave it in direct rain to improve tone
Tighten every part until it breaks
Share it without checking its condition
questions.correctAnswer: Clean it, store it safely, and protect it from dampness or damage
questions.explanation: Careful storage and cleaning preserve the instrument's tone and physical condition.
questions.learningOutcome: Handle and maintain selected indigenous musical instruments responsibly.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to perform music in the cultural idiom of an indigenous instrument?
options: Use style, technique, rhythm, and context associated with that instrument
Play any tune as loudly as possible
Avoid learning how the instrument is normally handled
Use only Western staff notation and no other knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: Use style, technique, rhythm, and context associated with that instrument
questions.explanation: Cultural idiom refers to the musical habits, techniques, and contexts that give an instrument its identity.
questions.learningOutcome: Perform music from the cultural idiom of a selected indigenous instrument.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to improve solo performance on a Kenyan flute. Which approach is strongest?
options: Practise tone production, fingering, breathing, style, and feedback from a knowledgeable player
Focus only on costume colour
Avoid listening to skilled performers
Change instrument every lesson before learning basics
questions.correctAnswer: Practise tone production, fingering, breathing, style, and feedback from a knowledgeable player
questions.explanation: Proficiency grows through focused technique, stylistic awareness, practice, and informed feedback.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop proficiency in solo indigenous instrumental performance.

questions.prompt: Which factor most clearly marks the cultural identity of an indigenous solo instrument performance?
options: Playing technique, repertoire, context, and associated movement or rhythm
The brand of the learner's phone
The colour of the classroom walls
The number of printed worksheets
questions.correctAnswer: Playing technique, repertoire, context, and associated movement or rhythm
questions.explanation: Cultural identity is shown through how the instrument is played, what is performed, and the context of performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse features that show cultural identity in indigenous instrumental performance.

questions.prompt: Which family does the trumpet belong to?
options: Brass
String
Woodwind
Membranophone
questions.correctAnswer: Brass
questions.explanation: The trumpet is a brass instrument because sound is produced by lip vibration into a metal tube.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify families of Western musical instruments.

questions.prompt: Why can two Western instruments play the same pitch but still sound different?
options: They have different tone colours caused by materials, shape, and playing method
They secretly play different notes
They always use different time signatures
They cannot play the same pitch in reality
questions.correctAnswer: They have different tone colours caused by materials, shape, and playing method
questions.explanation: Tone colour, or timbre, distinguishes instruments even when pitch and rhythm are the same.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe sound qualities of selected Western solo instruments.

questions.prompt: Which practice habit best develops proficiency on a selected Western solo instrument?
options: Regular focused practice with scales, technique, pieces, and reflection
Practising only on the morning of a concert
Avoiding warm-ups and tuning
Changing pieces whenever a hard passage appears
questions.correctAnswer: Regular focused practice with scales, technique, pieces, and reflection
questions.explanation: Instrumental proficiency grows from consistent technical practice and thoughtful review.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare a rehearsal schedule for a selected Western solo instrument.

questions.prompt: Before playing a violin or guitar in a school performance, what should a learner check first?
options: Tuning and safe instrument condition
The colour of the audience seats
Whether the title has exactly five words
If the piece can be played without rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: Tuning and safe instrument condition
questions.explanation: Tuning and instrument condition affect sound quality, safety, and confidence in performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Tune and care for a selected Western solo instrument.

questions.prompt: A recorder player squeaks often during rehearsal. Which technical area should be checked first?
options: Breath control and finger coverage
Costume length
Dance floor markings
Audience size
questions.correctAnswer: Breath control and finger coverage
questions.explanation: Wind instruments often squeak when breath pressure or finger sealing is not controlled.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply instrument-specific playing techniques.

questions.prompt: Which performance preparation best fits a school function solo on keyboard?
options: Practise fingering, rhythm, dynamics, pedalling where needed, and stage entry
Ignore rhythm because keys produce sound easily
Use the loudest volume for the whole piece
Avoid checking the power source until after performing
questions.correctAnswer: Practise fingering, rhythm, dynamics, pedalling where needed, and stage entry
questions.explanation: A keyboard solo needs technical control, musical expression, and practical stage preparation.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare and perform a solo piece on a selected Western instrument.

questions.prompt: Which review process best improves a Western solo instrumental performance?
options: Record a rehearsal, compare it with the score, note technical issues, and practise targeted sections
Listen once and decide no changes are possible
Ask only whether the instrument looks expensive
Practise only the easiest bars repeatedly
questions.correctAnswer: Record a rehearsal, compare it with the score, note technical issues, and practise targeted sections
questions.explanation: Focused review helps the performer connect evidence from rehearsal to specific improvements.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate and refine solo instrumental performance.

questions.prompt: Which feature is central to contemporary dance from Kenya in Grade 10 Music?
options: A storyline expressed through body movement and space
Only medieval plain song
A written chemistry formula
A silent score with no movement
questions.correctAnswer: A storyline expressed through body movement and space
questions.explanation: Contemporary dance often uses movement, space, and expression to communicate a story or issue.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe features of contemporary dance from Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which set lists basic performance skills used in contemporary dance?
options: Posture, alignment, balance, coordination, and control
Clef, stave, accidental, ledger, and bar line
Diction, vowel, consonant, aria, and breath
Tuning, fingering, reed, valve, and bow
questions.correctAnswer: Posture, alignment, balance, coordination, and control
questions.explanation: These physical skills help dancers move safely, expressively, and with control.
questions.learningOutcome: Execute basic performance skills in a dance routine.

questions.prompt: Which Kenyan popular music style can provide a suitable basis for a contemporary dance routine?
options: Benga
Plainchant only
Organum only
Silent recitation only
questions.correctAnswer: Benga
questions.explanation: Kenyan popular styles such as benga, genge, taarab, kapuka, rap, and hip-hop can support contemporary dance routines.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable Kenyan popular music for contemporary dance creation.

questions.prompt: Which performance technique is used in contemporary dance?
options: Fall and recovery
Writing a key signature
Tuning a trumpet valve
Adding a double bar line
questions.correctAnswer: Fall and recovery
questions.explanation: Fall and recovery is a movement technique where loss and regaining of balance become expressive material.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply contemporary dance performance techniques.

questions.prompt: A group wants to choreograph a dance about road safety. Which first step best supports the storyline?
options: Identify key events and messages before selecting movements
Start with random jumps and add meaning later
Choose the brightest costumes before knowing the theme
Avoid discussing the issue with the group
questions.correctAnswer: Identify key events and messages before selecting movements
questions.explanation: A clear storyline helps dancers choose movements that communicate the intended message.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a contemporary dance routine based on a Kenyan community issue.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows effective blocking in a contemporary dance routine?
options: Dancers are placed and moved so the audience can follow the action clearly
Every dancer stays hidden behind another dancer
Movements ignore the stage size
The group changes formations without rehearsal
questions.correctAnswer: Dancers are placed and moved so the audience can follow the action clearly
questions.explanation: Blocking organises positions and pathways so movement is visible, safe, and meaningful.
questions.learningOutcome: Use time, space, action, and energy effectively in choreography.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares a 3-5 minute contemporary dance routine for performance?
options: Choose Kenyan music, build a story, select techniques, plan formations, rehearse, and refine
Perform without deciding a theme
Use only one movement for five minutes
Avoid costumes, spacing, and feedback completely
questions.correctAnswer: Choose Kenyan music, build a story, select techniques, plan formations, rehearse, and refine
questions.explanation: A complete plan connects music, story, movement technique, staging, rehearsal, and improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create and perform a contemporary dance routine based on Kenyan popular music.

questions.prompt: In critical appreciation, what is performance media?
options: The voices, instruments, movement, and other means used to present a work
The price of a ticket only
The name of the classroom
The number of pages in a textbook
questions.correctAnswer: The voices, instruments, movement, and other means used to present a work
questions.explanation: Performance media are the resources through which a music or dance work is presented.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe performance media in Kenyan folk songs.

questions.prompt: Which feature would most likely show responsorial structure in a Kenyan folk song?
options: A leader sings a line and a group answers
A single keyboard plays without singers
All performers read silently
A melody has no repeated sections
questions.correctAnswer: A leader sings a line and a group answers
questions.explanation: Responsorial structure uses a leader's call followed by a group response.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify structural features of Kenyan folk songs.

questions.prompt: Which question best guides analysis of a Kenyan folk song's social function?
options: What occasion or community purpose does the song serve?
How many pixels are in the video recording?
Which software printed the title?
What colour is the storage folder?
questions.correctAnswer: What occasion or community purpose does the song serve?
questions.explanation: Social function is understood by linking the song to its purpose and performance context.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse functions of Kenyan folk songs in context.

questions.prompt: A folk-song performance includes a solo leader, chorus response, clapping, and dance. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The work combines vocal, rhythmic, and movement media
The work has no performance media
The song is automatically a Renaissance madrigal
The performance cannot be analysed
questions.correctAnswer: The work combines vocal, rhythmic, and movement media
questions.explanation: The listed features show several media working together in one performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse performance media in Kenyan folk songs.

questions.prompt: Which observation best connects folk-song lyrics to cultural meaning?
options: Repeated praise words show respect for a valued person or event
The words are unimportant if rhythm exists
All folk songs have the same meaning
Lyrics should be judged only by spelling length
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated praise words show respect for a valued person or event
questions.explanation: Lyrics can reveal values, occasion, relationships, and messages in a folk performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret meaning and values communicated in Kenyan folk songs.

questions.prompt: Which method gives the most balanced appreciation of a Kenyan folk-song performance?
options: Consider context, text, vocal style, instruments, movement, and audience role
Judge only the loudness of the drum
Ignore the purpose of the song
Describe costume colour without discussing music
questions.correctAnswer: Consider context, text, vocal style, instruments, movement, and audience role
questions.explanation: Balanced appreciation examines several musical, cultural, and performance features together.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse Kenyan folk songs using multiple appreciation criteria.

questions.prompt: Why is respectful language important when critiquing a folk-song performance from a community culture?
options: It recognises the dignity of performers and the value of cultural expression
It prevents all musical analysis
It means every performance must be called perfect
It avoids mentioning any observable feature
questions.correctAnswer: It recognises the dignity of performers and the value of cultural expression
questions.explanation: Critical appreciation should be honest while respecting people, culture, and artistic effort.
questions.learningOutcome: Give respectful feedback on Kenyan folk-song performances.

questions.prompt: Which genre is strongly associated with Medieval church music?
options: Plain song
Genge
Benga
Kapuka
questions.correctAnswer: Plain song
questions.explanation: Plain song, also called plainchant, is a Medieval sacred vocal genre.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify genres from the Medieval period.

questions.prompt: What is organum in Medieval music?
options: A form where an additional voice is added to a chant melody
A Kenyan drum pattern for harvest songs
A solo dance with no music
A modern audio file format
questions.correctAnswer: A form where an additional voice is added to a chant melody
questions.explanation: Organum developed by adding another vocal line to an existing chant.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe characteristics of Medieval music genres.

questions.prompt: Which genre is a secular Renaissance part-song often linked with expressive word setting?
options: Madrigal
Plain song
Organum
Drum signal
questions.correctAnswer: Madrigal
questions.explanation: The madrigal is a Renaissance secular vocal genre known for expressive text setting.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify genres from the Renaissance period.

questions.prompt: Which description best fits a Renaissance Mass?
options: A sacred musical setting of parts of the Christian liturgy
A short Kenyan popular dance routine
A solo instrumental warm-up only
A text message saved in notation software
questions.correctAnswer: A sacred musical setting of parts of the Christian liturgy
questions.explanation: A Mass is a sacred work based on liturgical texts, often set for voices.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe Renaissance sacred music genres.

questions.prompt: Which feature is common in Renaissance polyphony?
options: Independent vocal lines woven together
Only one spoken word with no pitch
No relationship between parts
Every piece using electronic drums
questions.correctAnswer: Independent vocal lines woven together
questions.explanation: Renaissance polyphony often uses several independent but related lines to create texture.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe characteristics of music in prescribed classical periods.

questions.prompt: A work is described as a keyboard-like instrumental piece with brilliant running passages. Which Renaissance genre could this suggest?
options: Toccata
Plain song
Work song
Lullaby
questions.correctAnswer: Toccata
questions.explanation: A toccata is an instrumental genre often associated with display and keyboard technique.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify Renaissance instrumental genres.

questions.prompt: Which comparison between Medieval plain song and a Renaissance madrigal is most accurate?
options: Plain song is generally monophonic and sacred, while a madrigal is often secular and polyphonic
Both are always Kenyan instrumental dances
Plain song uses only drums, while madrigal uses only whistles
Madrigals existed before all Medieval chant
questions.correctAnswer: Plain song is generally monophonic and sacred, while a madrigal is often secular and polyphonic
questions.explanation: The two genres differ in period, texture, function, and typical text treatment.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare characteristics of Medieval and Renaissance genres.

questions.prompt: Which is an educational function of music and dance in society?
options: Teaching values, history, or practical messages through performance
Removing communication from community events
Preventing learners from working together
Replacing all spoken language permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching values, history, or practical messages through performance
questions.explanation: Music and dance can pass knowledge, values, and social messages across generations.
questions.subStrandTitle: Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context
questions.learningOutcome: Explain functions of music and dance in society.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows an economic function of music and dance?
options: Artists earn income from performances, teaching, production, or cultural events
A song has no performers
A dance is never shared with anyone
A rhythm is written without any purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Artists earn income from performances, teaching, production, or cultural events
questions.explanation: Music and dance can support livelihoods through creative work and related services.
questions.subStrandTitle: Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context
questions.learningOutcome: Explain economic functions of music and dance in society.

questions.prompt: Which change shows how music performance practices can adapt over time?
options: Traditional songs being arranged with new instruments while retaining the core message
All communities stopping music permanently
Every performance losing rhythm
Dancers refusing to rehearse any movement
questions.correctAnswer: Traditional songs being arranged with new instruments while retaining the core message
questions.explanation: Performance practices may change in instrumentation, language, timing, or staging while retaining important meanings.
questions.subStrandTitle: Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context
questions.learningOutcome: Examine changing music and dance performance practices in different contexts.

questions.prompt: A school cultural event shortens a ceremonial song and adds stage lighting for a hall performance. Which issue should learners discuss?
options: How the new setting affects timing, message, audience, and presentation
Whether all music should be banned from halls
How to hide the performers from the audience
Why no rehearsal is needed after adaptation
questions.correctAnswer: How the new setting affects timing, message, audience, and presentation
questions.explanation: A changed context can affect how music is packaged, timed, staged, and understood.
questions.subStrandTitle: Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how context influences music and dance performances.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows responsible global citizenship in music and dance appreciation?
options: Respecting diverse cultures while analysing their performance practices thoughtfully
Mocking unfamiliar performance styles
Copying cultural items without acknowledgement
Refusing to learn from any other culture
questions.correctAnswer: Respecting diverse cultures while analysing their performance practices thoughtfully
questions.explanation: Responsible appreciation combines cultural respect, honest analysis, and acknowledgement of sources.
questions.subStrandTitle: Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context
questions.learningOutcome: Value diverse functions and contexts of music and dance.

questions.prompt: Which project best demonstrates Grade 10 understanding of music and dance in socio-cultural context?
options: Research a local performance, explain its function, note changing practices, and present respectful findings
List random song titles without context
Record a performance and ignore consent or source information
Describe only costumes without mentioning function or change
questions.correctAnswer: Research a local performance, explain its function, note changing practices, and present respectful findings
questions.explanation: A strong project connects research, function, changing practice, and respectful communication.
questions.subStrandTitle: Music and Dance in Socio-Cultural Context
questions.learningOutcome: Create a researched appreciation report on music and dance in socio-cultural context.
